segments.arabic: [800] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن الأعمش حدثني شقيق عن عبد الله قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from al-A‘mash: Shaqiq related to me, from ‘Abdullah, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا إذا كنا مع النبي ﷺ في الصلاة قلنا السلام على الله من عباده السلام على فلان وفلان، فقال النبي ﷺ لا تقولوا السلام على الله فإن الله هو السلام ولكن قولوا التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين فإنكم إذا قلتم أصاب كل عبد في السماء أو بين السماء والأرض أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله ثم يتخير من الدعاء أعجبه إليه فيدعو
segments.english: When we were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in prayer, we used to say, “Peace be upon Allah from His servants. Peace be upon so-and-so and so-and-so.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Do not say, ‘Peace be upon Allah,’ for Allah is Peace. Instead say: ‘Greetings belong to Allah, and prayers and good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and Allah’s mercy and blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah’s righteous servants.’ When you say this, it reaches every servant in heaven or between heaven and earth. ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger.’ Then he chooses whichever supplication he likes best and supplicates.”

notes: The selected order of greetings, prayers and good things remains. Every servant and the or between the two locations are retained without adding righteous or replacing or with and. The historical print adds ذلك and a final به; these are not inserted.

segments.arabic: [801] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة قال: سألت أبا سعيد الخدري، فقال:
segments.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said: I asked Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, and he said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يسجد في الماء والطين حتى رأيت أثر الطين في جبهته
segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrating in water and mud, until I saw the trace of mud on his forehead.

notes: The question in the chain and water-before-mud order remain. Both Arabic prints include a separate Abu Abdullah/Al-Humaydi chapter comment absent from the selected digital chapter; it is not silently appended to this numbered report.

segments.arabic: [802] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد حدثنا الزهري عن هند بنت الحارث أن أم سلمة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. Al-Zuhri related to us, from Hind bint al-Harith: Umm Salamah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا سلم قام النساء حين يقضي تسليمه ومكث يسيرا قبل أن يقوم
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said the closing greeting, the women would rise as soon as he finished saying it. He remained a little while before rising.

segments.arabic: قال ابن شهاب فأرى والله أعلم أن مكثه لكي ينفذ النساء قبل أن يدركهن من انصرف من القوم
segments.english: Ibn Shihab said: I think—and Allah knows best—that he remained so the women could leave before those of the people who departed caught up with them.

notes: I think and Allah knows best remain narrator commentary. People is retained without narrowing it to men from a comparison translation.

segments.arabic: [803] حدثنا حبان بن موسى قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا معمر عن الزهري عن محمود بن الربيع عن عتبان قال
segments.english: Hibban ibn Musa related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, from ‘Itban, who said:

segments.arabic: صلينا مع النبي ﷺ فسلمنا حين سلم
segments.english: We prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said the closing greeting when he said it.

notes: Hibban follows the inspected vocalisation. The historical print expands Itban to Ibn Malik and inserts huwa into Mahmud’s name; the selected shorter wording remains.

segments.arabic: [804] حدثنا عبدان قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا معمر عن الزهري قال: أخبرني محمود بن الربيع وزعم أنه عقل رسول الله ﷺ وعقل مجة مجها من دلو كان في دارهم قال: سمعت عتبان بن مالك الأنصارى ثم أحد بني سالم قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ informed me. He stated that he remembered the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and remembered a mouthful of water that he spat out from a bucket that was in their house. He said: I heard ‘Itban ibn Malik al-Ansari, one of Banu Salim, say:

segments.arabic: كنت أصلي لقومي بني سالم فأتيت النبي ﷺ فقلت: إني أنكرت بصري وإن السيول تحول بيني وبين مسجد قومي فلوددت أنك جئت فصليت في بيتي مكانا حتى اتخذه مسجدا، فقال افعل إن شاء الله فغدا على رسول الله ﷺ وأبو بكر معه بعد ما أشتد النهار فأستأذن النبي ﷺ فأذنت له فلم يجلس حتى قال أين تحب أن أصلي من بيتك فأشار إليه من المكان الذي أحب أن يصلي فيه فقام فصففنا خلفه ثم سلم وسلمنا حين سلم
segments.english: I used to lead my people, Banu Salim, in prayer. I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “I have noticed my eyesight failing, and the floods come between me and my people’s mosque. I would like you to come and pray in a place in my house so I can take it as a place of prayer.” He said, “I will do so, if Allah wills.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to me in the morning, with Abu Bakr accompanying him, after the day had grown intense. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked permission to enter, and I gave him permission. He did not sit down before saying, “Where in your house would you like me to pray?” He pointed out to him the place where he wanted him to pray. He stood, and we formed rows behind him. Then he said the closing greeting, and we said it when he said it.

notes: The recollection of the bucket and mouthful remains; on me is not supplied. The selected third-person he pointed remains, rather than changing it to I pointed as in the English comparisons. The modern print labels the recollection and ensuing account separately as 839 and 840; this selected report retains both.

segments.arabic: [805] حدثنا إسحاق بن نصر قال: حدثنا عبد الرزاق قال: أخبرنا ابن جريج قال: أخبرني عمرو أن أبا معبد مولى ابن عباس أخبره ان ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أخبره
segments.english: Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: ‘Amr informed me that Abu Ma‘bad, a client of Ibn ‘Abbas, informed him that Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رفع الصوت بالذكر حين ينصرف الناس من المكتوبة كان على عهد النبي ﷺ، وقال ابن عباس كنت أعلم إذا انصرفوا بذلك إذا سمعته
segments.english: Raising the voice in remembrance when people departed from the obligatory prayer took place in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Ibn ‘Abbas said: I used to know when they had departed by hearing it.

notes: Every informed-me/informed-him link remains. Remembrance is not narrowed to a particular formula.

segments.arabic: [806] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا عمرو قال: أخبرني أبو معبد عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: ‘Amr related to us. He said: Abu Ma‘bad informed me, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

segments.arabic: كنت أعرف انقضاء صلاة النبي ﷺ بالتكبير
segments.english: I used to recognise the completion of the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, by the takbir.

notes: Both Arabic prints include Amr and his transmission link, omitted from the digital chain. The explicit correction preserves the original and both exact page witnesses. The historical print also has a further Ali–Sufyan–Amr note naming Abu Ma‘bad; that addition is absent from the selected text and modern print and is not inserted.

segments.arabic: [807] حدثنا محمد بن أبي بكر قال: حدثنا معتمر عن عبيد الله عن سمي عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: جاء الفقراء إلى النبي ﷺ فقالوا ذهب أهل الدثور من الأموال بالدرجات العلا والنعيم المقيم يصلون كما نصلي ويصومون كما نصوم ولهم فضل من أموال يحجون بها ويعتمرون ويجاهدون ويتصدقون قال ألا أحدثكم بأمر إن أخذتم به أدركتم من سبقكم ولم يدرككم أحد بعدكم وكنتم خير من أنتم بين ظهرانيه إلا من عمل مثله تسبحون وتحمدون وتكبرون خلف كل صلاة ثلاثا وثلاثين
segments.english: The poor came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “Those with abundant wealth have taken the high ranks and lasting bliss. They pray as we pray and fast as we fast, but they have surplus wealth with which they perform Hajj and ‘Umrah, strive in jihad and give charity.” He said, “Shall I tell you of something which, if you take it up, will let you catch up with those who preceded you, and no one after you will catch up with you, and you will be the best of those among whom you live, except someone who does the same? You glorify Allah, praise Him and declare His greatness after every prayer, thirty-three times.”

segments.arabic: فاختلفنا بيننا، فقال بعضنا نسبح ثلاثا وثلاثين ونحمد ثلاثا وثلاثين ونكبر أربعا وثلاثين فرجعت إليه، فقال تقول سبحان الله والحمد لله والله أكبر حتى يكون منهن كلهن ثلاثا وثلاثين
segments.english: We disagreed among ourselves. Some of us said, “We glorify thirty-three times, praise thirty-three times and declare His greatness thirty-four times.” I went back to him, and he said, “You say, ‘Glory be to Allah,’ ‘Praise belongs to Allah,’ and ‘Allah is greatest,’ until all of them are thirty-three.”

notes: All four uses of surplus wealth and all stated counts remain. The selected final I went back to him does not name the person approached. Ibn Hajar discusses the apparent Abu Hurayrah attribution and a route explicitly identifying Sumayy returning to Abu Salih. The Khan-family insertion I went to the Prophet is not imported.

The Arabic leaves the distribution of the opening and closing thirty-three implicit. Classical commentary discusses different constructions; each and eleven are not inserted into the selected wording. The intervening thirty-three/thirty-three/thirty-four disagreement remains intact.

segments.arabic: [808] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال: حدثنا سفيان عن عبد الملك بن عمير عن وراد كاتب المغيرة بن شعبة قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, from Warrad, the secretary of al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, who said:

segments.arabic: أملى على المغيرة بن شعبة في كتاب إلى معاوية أن النبي ﷺ كان يقول: في دبر كل صلاة مكتوبة لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير اللهم لا مانع لما أعطيت ولا معطي لما منعت ولا ينفع ذا الجد منك الجد،
segments.english: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah dictated to me in a letter to Mu‘awiyah that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say after every obligatory prayer: “There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion, and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold, and wealth does not benefit the wealthy person against You.”

segments.arabic: وقال شعبة عن عبد الملك بهذا عن الحكم عن القاسم بن مخيمرة عن وراد بهذا، وقال الحسن الجد غنى
segments.english: Shu‘bah said, from ‘Abd al-Malik, with this report; from al-Hakam, from al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Warrad, with this report. Al-Hasan said: Jadd means wealth.

notes: The complete closing Shubah/Abd al-Malik and Hakam/Qasim/Warrad routes remain. Al-Qastallani explains the Hakam route as another route from Shubah, rather than Hakam being Abd al-Malik’s source. The selected text lacks an explicit conjunction before Hakam; a semicolon separates the routes without adding a narrator.

Al-Hasan’s lexical gloss remains last, as in the selected text and modern print; the historical print puts it between the two routes. Wealth follows this gloss; interpretive additions concerning effort or worship are not imported.

segments.arabic: [809] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا جرير بن حازم قال: حدثنا أبو رجاء عن سمرة بن جندب قال:
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Jarir ibn Hazim related to us. He said: Abu Raja’ related to us, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ إذا صلى صلاة أقبل علينا بوجهه
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had prayed a prayer, he turned his face towards us.

notes: The complete named chain and the unspecified a prayer remain. No particular prayer or additional address is supplied from another report.

segments.arabic: [810] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن صالح بن كيسان عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود عن زيد بن خالد الجهني أنه قال
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى لنا رسول الله ﷺ صلاة الصبح بالحديبية على إثر سماء كانت من الليلة فلما انصرف أقبل على الناس، فقال هل تدرون ماذا قال ربكم قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال أصبح من عبادي مؤمن بي وكافر فأما من قال مطرنا بفضل الله ورحمته فذلك مؤمن بي وكافر بالكوكب وأما من قال بنوء كذا وكذا فذلك كافر بي ومؤمن بالكوكب
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in the dawn prayer at al-Hudaybiyah after rain during the night. When he finished, he turned towards the people and said, “Do you know what your Lord said?” They said, “Allah and His messenger know best.” He said, “Among My servants this morning are a believer in Me and a disbeliever. As for whoever said, ‘We were given rain by Allah’s favour and mercy,’ that person believes in Me and disbelieves in the star. But whoever said, ‘By the naw’ of such-and-such a star,’ that person disbelieves in Me and believes in the star.”

notes: Both inspected prints include بي after the first مؤمن. This exact printed reading is recorded as a correction with the original retained. The later elliptical By such-and-such wording remains without importing an additional We were given rain.

Naw’ is retained as a technical word: the setting of one of the relevant stars, or the rising of its counterpart, and its associated period. A separate lexical note gives this meaning; no legal ruling is added. The historical print’s additional عز وجل is not imported.

segments.arabic: [811] حدثنا عبد الله سمع يزيد قال: أخبرنا حميد عن أنس قال
segments.english: ‘Abdullah related to us; he heard Yazid, who said: Humayd informed us, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: أخر رسول الله ﷺ الصلاة ذات ليلة إلى شطر الليل ثم خرج علينا فلما صلى أقبل علينا بوجهه، فقال إن الناس قد صلوا ورقدوا وإنكم لن تزالوا في صلاة ما انتظرتم الصلاة
segments.english: One night the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed the prayer until half the night had passed. Then he came out to us. When he had prayed, he turned his face towards us and said, “The people have prayed and gone to sleep, but you will remain in prayer as long as you wait for the prayer.”

notes: The selected short Abdullah, Yazid and Anas names remain; the historical print expands them. The prayer is unnamed in the selected wording, so Isha is not inserted.

segments.arabic: [812] حدثنا أبو الوليد حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد حدثنا الزهري عن هند بنت الحارث عن أم سلمة
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. Al-Zuhri related to us, from Hind bint al-Harith, from Umm Salamah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا سلم يمكث في مكانه يسيرا
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said the closing greeting, he would remain in his place a little while.

segments.arabic: قال ابن شهاب فنرى والله أعلم لكي ينفذ من ينصرف من النساء،
segments.english: Ibn Shihab said: We think—and Allah knows best—that this was so those of the women who were leaving could depart.

segments.arabic: وقال ابن أبي مريم أخبرنا نافع بن يزيد قال: أخبرني جعفر بن ربيعة ان ابن شهاب كتب إليه قال: حدثتني هند بنت الحارث الفراسية عن أم سلمة زوج النبي ﷺ وكانت من صواحباتها قالت
segments.english: Ibn Abi Maryam said: Nafi‘ ibn Yazid informed us. He said: Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah informed me that Ibn Shihab wrote to him, saying: Hind bint al-Harith al-Firasiyyah related to me, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and she was one of her companions—who said:

segments.arabic: كان يسلم فينصرف النساء فيدخلن بيوتهن من قبل أن ينصرف رسول الله ﷺ،
segments.english: He would say the closing greeting, and the women would leave and enter their homes before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, departed.

segments.arabic: وقال ابن وهب عن يونس عن ابن شهاب أخبرتني هند الفراسية، وقال عثمان بن عمر أخبرنا يونس عن الزهري حدثتني هند الفراسية، وقال الزبيدي أخبرني الزهري أن هند بنت الحارث القرشية أخبرته وكانت تحت معبد بن المقداد وهو حليف بني زهرة وكانت تدخل على أزواج النبي ﷺ، وقال شعيب عن الزهري حدثتني هند القرشية، وقال ابن أبي عتيق عن الزهري عن هند الفراسية، وقال الليث حدثني يحيى بن سعيد حدثه عن ابن شهاب عن امرأة من قريش حدثته عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Ibn Wahb said, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab: Hind al-Firasiyyah informed me. ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri: Hind al-Firasiyyah related to me. Al-Zubaydi said: Al-Zuhri informed me that Hind bint al-Harith al-Qurashiyyah informed him. She was married to Ma‘bad ibn al-Miqdad, who was an ally of Banu Zuhrah, and she used to visit the wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Shu‘ayb said, from al-Zuhri: Hind al-Qurashiyyah related to me. Ibn Abi ‘Atiq said, from al-Zuhri, from Hind al-Firasiyyah. Al-Layth said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to me; he related to him from Ibn Shihab, from a woman of Quraysh who related to him from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: All eight named routes, both accounts, five prophetic honorifics, the written transmission and the marriage/alliance detail remain. The informed/related distinctions and Firasiyyah/Qurashiyyah identifications are not collapsed. The historical print calls Hind Qurashiyyah in Uthman’s route, where the selected text and modern print say Firasiyyah.

We think stays plural, unlike the I think of 802. The modern print separates labels 849 and 850; the selected complete report retains both. The Khan-family comparison omits the full closing variants, and Bewley condenses them into a general variations note; neither is used to abridge the Arabic.

segments.arabic: [813] حدثنا محمد بن عبيد قال: حدثنا عيسى بن يونس عن عمر بن سعيد قال: أخبرني ابن أبي مليكة عن عقبة قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd related to us. He said: ‘Isa ibn Yunus related to us, from ‘Umar ibn Sa‘id, who said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me, from ‘Uqbah, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت وراء النبي ﷺ بالمدينة العصر فسلم ثم قام مسرعا فتخطى رقاب الناس إلى بعض حجر نسائه ففزع الناس من سرعته فخرج عليهم فرأى أنهم عجبوا من سرعته، فقال: ذكرت شيئا من تبر عندنا فكرهت أن يحبسني فأمرت بقسمته
segments.english: I prayed the afternoon prayer behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in Madinah. He said the closing greeting, then rose quickly and stepped over the people’s necks towards one of his wives’ rooms. The people were startled by his haste. He came out to them and saw that they were surprised by his haste, so he said, “I remembered some uncoined gold we had. I disliked its holding me back, so I ordered it to be distributed.”

notes: The selected short Muhammad ibn Ubayd and Uqbah remain. Holding me back is retained without supplying a particular activity from which he would be detained.

segments.arabic: [814] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة عن سليمان عن عمارة بن عمير عن الأسود قال: قال عبد الله
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sulayman, from ‘Umarah ibn ‘Umayr, from al-Aswad, who said: ‘Abdullah said:

segments.arabic: لا يجعل أحدكم للشيطان شيئا من صلاته يرى أن حقا عليه أن لا ينصرف إلا عن يمينه لقد رأيت النبي ﷺ كثيرا ينصرف عن يساره
segments.english: None of you should give Satan a share of his prayer by thinking that he is obliged to depart only to his right. I have often seen the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, depart to his left.

notes: The selected related to us remains where the historical print has informed us. The frequency and left/right contrast remain without turning the report into an added practice instruction.

segments.arabic: [815] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن عبيد الله قال: حدثني نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن النبي ﷺ قال في غزوة خيبر
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, who said: Nafi‘ related to me, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said during the expedition of Khaybar:

segments.arabic: من أكل من هذه الشجرة يعني الثوم فلا يقربن مسجدنا
segments.english: Whoever eats from this plant—meaning garlic—must not approach our mosque.

notes: Meaning garlic is retained as an aside, rather than presented as a separate spoken command. The historical print places the following Jabir report before this one; the selected order and modern print are retained.

segments.arabic: [816] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا أبو عاصم قال: أخبرنا ابن جريج قال: أخبرني عطاء قال: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Asim related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: ‘Ata’ informed me. He said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: من أكل من هذه الشجرة يريد الثوم فلا يغشانا في مساجدنا
segments.english: Whoever eats from this plant—he means garlic—must not come to us in our mosques.

segments.arabic: قلت: ما يعني به قال: ما أراه يعني إلا نيئه، وقال مخلد بن يزيد عن ابن جريج إلا نتنه
segments.english: I asked, “What does he mean by it?” He said, “I only think he means it raw.” Makhlad ibn Yazid said, from Ibn Jurayj: “Only its foul smell.”

notes: The plural our mosques, I think uncertainty and complete Makhlad/Ibn Jurayj closing variant remain. Bewley places some compiler material belonging to 817 near this entry; it is not duplicated here.

segments.arabic: [817] حدثنا سعيد بن عفير قال: حدثنا ابن وهب عن يونس عن ابن شهاب زعم عطاء أن جابر بن عبد الله زعم أن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab: ‘Ata’ stated that Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah stated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: من أكل ثوما أو بصلا فليعتزلنا أو قال: فليعتزل مسجدنا وليقعد في بيته وأن النبي ﷺ أتي بقدر فيه خضرات من بقول فوجد لها ريحا فسأل فأخبر بما فيها من البقول، فقال قربوها إلى بعض أصحابه كان معه فلما رآه كره أكلها قال كل فإني أناجي من لا تناجي،
segments.english: “Whoever eats garlic or onions should keep away from us”; or he said, “Should keep away from our mosque and stay in his house.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought a pot containing green vegetables. He noticed a smell from them, asked about it and was told what vegetables it contained. He said, “Bring it near,” to one of his companions who was with him. When he saw it, he disliked eating it. He said, “Eat, for I converse privately with those with whom you do not converse.”

segments.arabic: وقال أحمد بن صالح عن ابن وهب أتي ببدر قال ابن وهب يعني طبقا فيه خضرات ولم يذكر الليث وأبو صفوان عن يونس قصة القدر فلا أدري هو من قول الزهري أو في الحديث، وقال أحمد بن صالح بعد حديث يونس عن ابن شهاب وهو يثبت قول يونس
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Salih said, from Ibn Wahb: He was brought a badr. Ibn Wahb said: Meaning a platter containing greens. Al-Layth and Abu Safwan did not mention the story of the pot from Yunus. I do not know whether it is a statement of al-Zuhri or part of the hadith. Ahmad ibn Salih said, after Yunus’s report from Ibn Shihab: He confirms Yunus’s statement.

notes: The two stated links, garlic OR onions, leave us OR our mosque, AND stay at home, and the final uncertainty are retained. The unnamed pronouns in the food scene are not replaced with a named companion, and angels is not inserted.

The final Ahmad ibn Salih clause is absent from both inspected print bodies. Al-Qastallani records its wording and its omission in named transmitted versions; the selected digital clause remains as an attested variant. Its elliptical attribution is not silently expanded.

segments.arabic: [818] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث عن عبد العزيز قال
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, who said:

segments.arabic: سأل رجل أنسا ما سمعت نبي الله ﷺ يذكر في الثوم، فقال: قال النبي ﷺ من أكل من هذه الشجرة فلا يقربنا أو لا يصلين معنا
segments.english: A man asked Anas, “What did you hear Allah’s Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mention about garlic?” He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Whoever eats from this plant must not come near us, or must not pray with us.”

notes: The selected mention is retained where the prints use say. The alternative OR remains, rather than the neither/nor of the Khan-family comparison. Anas is not expanded to Ibn Malik. The physical paragraph shared with 817 is not treated as one report.
